screenplay.text:
THE BORROWED BICYCLE

                                     Written by

                                 The Panelwise team






























               Self-written sample screenplay for Panelwise.
               Licence: Apache-2.0, the same as the repository.













               FADE IN:

               EXT. DUSTY YARD - DAY

               A small yard behind a brick house. Chickens peck at the
               ground. Against the fence leans a shining BLUE BICYCLE with
               a silver bell.

               NALEDI (12), dungarees, scraped knees, stares at it. Her
               little brother TSHEPO (8), shorts down past his knees,
               stands beside her.

                                     NALEDI
                         It's Mr. Kekana's. He said nobody
                         touches it.

                                     TSHEPO
                         He's at church until twelve.

                                     NALEDI
                         That's not the point.

               Tshepo rings the bell. Ting-ting. They both freeze and look
               at the house.

               Nothing happens.

                                     NALEDI
                         One ride. Around the block. Then
                         straight back.

               EXT. GRAVEL ROAD - MOMENTS LATER

               Naledi pedals standing up. Tshepo sits on the carrier behind
               her, arms around her waist, screaming with joy. Dust flies
               up from the wheels.

                                     TSHEPO
                         Faster! Faster!

               They fly past a SPAZA SHOP. The SHOPKEEPER (60s) looks up
               from his newspaper.

                                     SHOPKEEPER
                         Is that Kekana's bicycle?

                                     NALEDI
                               (over her shoulder)
                         No!

               EXT. HILL ROAD - DAY

               The road tips downhill. The bicycle picks up speed. Naledi
               squeezes the brakes. Nothing.








                                                                       2.


                                     NALEDI
                         The brakes don't work!

                                     TSHEPO
                         Why would he have a bicycle with no
                         brakes?

                                     NALEDI
                         Maybe that's why nobody touches it!

               At the bottom of the hill, a big muddy PUDDLE.

               EXT. BOTTOM OF THE HILL - CONTINUOUS

               SPLASH. The bicycle hits the puddle and stops dead. Naledi
               and Tshepo tumble sideways into the mud.

               They sit up, brown from head to toe. The bicycle lies on its
               side, its front wheel still spinning.

               Tshepo starts to laugh. Naledi tries not to, and fails.

               EXT. DUSTY YARD - LATER

               Naledi scrubs the bicycle with a bucket and a rag. Tshepo
               polishes the bell with the hem of his shirt.

               The bicycle shines again. The two children, however, are
               still covered in mud.

               The back door opens. MR. KEKANA (70s), in a church suit and
               a hat with a feather, steps out. He looks at the bicycle. He
               looks at the children.

                                     MR. KEKANA
                         You went down the hill.

                                     NALEDI
                         How did you know?

                                     MR. KEKANA
                         Because that's where I went, fifty
                         years ago, the day I got it. The
                         brakes have never worked since.

               He takes off his hat and hangs it on the handlebars.

                                     MR. KEKANA
                         Next Sunday, I'll show you how to
                         fix them. Then you can borrow it
                         properly.

                                     TSHEPO
                         Can we ride it now?








                                                                       3.


                                     MR. KEKANA
                               (pointing at a tap)
                         Now you wash.

                                                            FADE OUT.
